_about: EA Explorer's on-screen help (D497): one catalogue for help panels and tooltips. Keys: page:#/route, tab:Label, popup:Title (* for the dynamic parts), step:Label, field:Label, button:Text. Pages, tabs, pop-ups and steps hold {title?, what, how[], example?}; fields and buttons hold the tooltip text. How to add help: docs/help-catalogue.md. tools/help_inventory.py lists what is missing.

page:#/.title: Start
page:#/.what: Home: the start page. Everything else is in the menu bar's nine areas (User, Architecture Work, Model Admin, Project Admin, Repository, Documentation, Profile, System Admin, Farm Admin); press / to find any function or content.
how: Pick an area card to go there; the top bar takes you to the same areas from any page.
Your tasks, notifications (the bell) and your last model and project are always at the top.
Ctrl+K opens Quick jump: type a few letters of a model, project or tab to go straight there.
page:#/.example: Click Architecture work, then a project, to carry on where you left off.

page:#/admin.title: System admin
page:#/admin.what: Running the installation: settings, users, health, containers, backups, restores, quality, machine access and operations.
how: Choose a tab; most need the Super Admin or IT Admin role.
Changes to settings are kept with who made them and when.
Anything that restarts or restores asks you to confirm first.
page:#/admin.example: Health › Recalculate after a restore, to check every service is up.

page:#/break-glass.title: Break-glass sign-in
page:#/break-glass.what: The emergency way in when the normal sign-in (Keycloak) is down.
how: Use the break-glass password kept by your IT team.
Everything you do is logged as break-glass; sign out as soon as the normal sign-in works again.
page:#/break-glass.example: Keycloak will not start after an upgrade: sign in here, check Health and restart it.

page:#/change-documents.title: Change documents
page:#/change-documents.what: Documents that record a change to a model's metamodel or content: what was asked, decided and done.
how: Open one to read it, comment or approve it if you are asked to.
Filter by model or status to find the one you need.
page:#/change-documents.example: The change document for adding the Product type to Claims 2028.

page:#/change-log.title: Change log
page:#/change-log.what: Every change made in EA Explorer: who, when, what, before and after.
how: Filter by model, person, kind of change or words; open an entry to see its details.
Super Admins can delete old entries (kept per the retention rules).
page:#/change-log.example: Search 'Claims Platform' to see everyone who changed it this month.

page:#/compare.title: Compare
page:#/compare.what: Compare two models, or one model at two moments (tags), and see what was added, changed and removed.
how: Choose the baseline (left) and the target (right), then Compare.
Save a comparison as a gap analysis to keep it; Common analysis finds what several models share.
page:#/compare.example: Baseline 2026 against Target 2028 of the claims model.

page:#/enterprise-library.title: Enterprise library
page:#/enterprise-library.what: Your organisation's own reference content: principles, standards, templates and reference models to reuse in projects.
how: Browse or search; open an item to see it and where it is used.
Library Admins add and change items; everyone can use them.
page:#/enterprise-library.example: Find the 'Reuse before buy' principle and add it to a project.

page:#/library.title: Library
page:#/library.what: The model library: the reference and template models you can start new models from.
how: Open a model to look at it; use it as the base of a new model from the Models page or a project.
Frozen and archived models are hidden until you tick Show frozen and archived.
page:#/library.example: Open the Retail reference model 1.0 and look at its capability map.

page:#/project-library.title: Project library
page:#/project-library.what: The library projects: reference material every project can use (reference models, regulations, patterns, standards, useful links). Everyone with a role reads them.
how: Open a library project to read its Reference area.
A new project copies what it needs from here (New project › Reference).
A Super Admin makes a project a library project here, or stops one being a library project.
page:#/project-library.example: Open the library project and look at the regulations in its Reference area.

page:#/maturity.title: EA capability maturity
page:#/maturity.what: How mature the organisation's architecture practice is: assessments answered by chosen people, scored 0 to 5 per area, with evidence EA Explorer measures itself.
how: Super Admins create an assessment, choose who answers and send it.
People answer in a table: pick a level 0 to 5 per area, add a comment and evidence links; the bar fills as you choose.
Results (Super Admins only): the mean per area with the target, the gap and the previous assessment; the overall weighted score; each person's answers.
page:#/maturity.example: November 2026: governance 2.4 against a target of 3, up from 1.8 in May.

page:#/mcp.title: MCP
page:#/mcp.what: Connecting an AI assistant (your own language model) to EA Explorer through the Model Context Protocol.
how: Connect: the address and how to add EA Explorer as a connector in your AI app.
AI activity: every call the assistant made for you (admins see everyone's).
Tools: what the assistant can do; anything that changes something shows a preview and needs your confirmation.
page:#/mcp.example: Ask the assistant: 'make a copy of Claims 2028 and remove the duplicates'.

page:#/merge-requests.title: Merge requests
page:#/merge-requests.what: Children sent for merge into a parent model that are waiting for you, and your own requests.
how: Open a request to review it change by change: accept, or reject with a reason.
When every change is decided, Merge puts the accepted ones into the parent as one commit.
page:#/merge-requests.example: Fynbos Commercial sent for merge with one conflict to decide.

page:#/metamodel.title: Models
page:#/metamodel.what: Every model you can see, and each model's page with its content, views, quality, reports and metamodel.
how: Pick a model from the list or the Model box in the top bar.
On a model, the tabs are grouped (Content, Views, Quality, Reports, Metamodel, Manage); ▦ beside your name changes how tabs are shown.
Right-click an entity row for Open, Edit, History, Add to a view and more.
page:#/metamodel.example: Protea Insurance (demo estate) › Content › Grid to see every application.

page:#/model-admin.title: Model admin
page:#/model-admin.what: Every model wizard and admin task for one model: copy, merge, freeze, split, extend, people, tags, backups.
how: Wizards: pick the job; each wizard explains itself and asks before changing anything.
Changes: merges, merge requests, push down and change documents.
Admin: metamodel, people, tags, backups and the family of the model.
page:#/model-admin.example: Wizards › Send for merge into the parent, after finishing the 2028 target.

page:#/more.title: Everything else
page:#/more.what: Pages that are not part of daily architecture work: surveys, notifications, your profile, change documents and more.
how: Pick a card to open the page.
page:#/more.example: Surveys, to answer the repository-use survey.

page:#/documentation.title: Documentation
page:#/documentation.what: Every document that ships with the version of EA Explorer you are using: getting started, using it, running it, the command line, reference and how it was designed. The same documents are in the Enterprise library, folder EA Explorer documentation.
how: Choose a document from its group to read it here; links between documents open them in place.
Type in Search all documents to find every document holding all your words.
In a document, Download gives its own file and Print or save as PDF prints it.
page:#/documentation.example: Search 'housekeeping dry run' to find how old records are archived.

page:#/drawio/open.title: A picture in draw.io
page:#/drawio/open.what: A generated picture, a canvas, the metamodel diagram or a .drawio document, opened in our own draw.io to look at and export. It is kept nowhere and changes nothing in the model.
how: Zoom and look; draw.io's File › Export as offers .drawio file, PNG, SVG and PDF.
Download .drawio, PNG, SVG or PDF from the bar at the top.
To keep it or change it: Save as a drawn view (if you may draw on the model). The tab becomes that drawn view.
Close asks first: Leave without saving? This picture isn't kept. A reload of the tab keeps it (very large pictures excepted: the tab says so).

page:#/my-profile.title: My profile
how: Add your skills so project leads can find you.
Press / (or Ctrl+K) anywhere to find a function or content.

page:#/notifications.title: Notifications
page:#/notifications.what: Messages for you: things to do (approve, review, answer) and things you may want to know.
how: Open one to act on it; done items move to the finished list.
Requests to me and Requests I sent show the asks between people.
page:#/notifications.example: A merge request waits for your review.

page:#/project-admin.title: Project admin
page:#/project-admin.what: Setting up and changing projects: templates, libraries and project settings.
how: Pick a project to change it, or a template to change how new projects start.
page:#/project-admin.example: Change the Transformation template's default phases.

page:#/projects.title: Projects
page:#/projects.what: Architecture projects: each runs one ADM cycle or a piece of architecture work with its models, people, deliverables and sign-off.
how: Open a project; its tabs are grouped as Overview, Plan, Business, Architecture, Governance and Documents.
+ New project starts the guided wizard.

page:#/reference-library.title: Reference library
page:#/reference-library.what: Published reference material: frameworks and reference models, to read and reuse.
how: Browse the areas or search; open an item to read it or link to it from a project.
page:#/reference-library.example: Find the capability map of the Healthcare reference model.

page:#/repository.title: Architecture repository
page:#/repository.what: The organisation's architecture repository: architecture capability, landscape, standards, reference library and governance in one place.
how: Pick an area card; each lists what the repository holds there and where it lives in EA Explorer.
page:#/repository.example: Architecture capability › Maturity, to see the last assessment.

page:#/search.title: Search
page:#/search.what: Find anything: entities in every model you can read, by name, ID, description, tag or value.
how: Type at least two letters; narrow by model or type; open a result to go to it.

page:#/surveys.title: Surveys
page:#/surveys.what: Questionnaires sent to people through their task list: what to answer, what you answered and the surveys you run.
how: To answer: open one and answer; required questions are marked.
I run: design a survey (sections, questions, conditions), choose who answers, send, remind and close; see the results and download Excel.
Answers never change any model.
page:#/surveys.example: Ask the architects five questions about how they use the repository.

page:#/work.title: Architecture work
page:#/work.what: Your projects and the models you work in, with what needs you.
how: Open a project or model; pinned ones stay at the top.

tab:AI activity.what: Every MCP call made for you by an AI assistant: the tool, your question, how much came back, what changed, and links to the changes.
how: Filter by kind (read, preview, change, refused, error). Admins see everyone's calls.
tab:AI activity.example: A merge done through MCP shows as a change with links to the entities.

tab:All.what: Everything in this list, without a filter.
how: Pick another tab to narrow the list.

tab:All phases.what: Every ADM phase of the project with its steps and deliverables.
how: Open a phase to see its steps; tick steps as they are done.

tab:Allowed relationships.what: What the metamodel allows for the selected shape's type, both ways, with the other types and how many.
how: Click one to add a connected placeholder; a pop-up then asks whether to bind it to an existing entity, create one or leave it.
Open one to read your answers; while it is open you may change them.

tab:Application settings.what: Settings everyone sees: formats, time zone, names, the start page and the parts switched on.
how: Change a value and Save; earlier values are kept.
tab:Application settings.example: Set the date format to 10 Nov 2026.

tab:Background tasks.what: Long jobs running in the background: loads, backups, copies, reports.
how: Open a task to see its progress and log; finished ones can be cleared.

tab:Backups.what: Backups: infrastructure (every database and file) and application (every model as a file).
how: Back up now, see the schedule, download or restore a backup; pinned backups are never removed.
tab:Backups.example: Back up now before an upgrade.

tab:Base.what: What the project starts from: the baseline models and their tags.
how: Choose the models the project builds on and the moment (tag) they are taken from.

tab:Business artifacts.what: Business architecture deliverables of the project: canvases, maps and catalogues.
how: Open an artifact to fill it in; ready ones can be sent for sign-off.

tab:Business model canvas.what: The project's business model canvases: nine boxes of how the organisation creates value.
how: + New canvas, then fill each box; link boxes to entities in the model.

tab:Business views.what: Ready-made business views of the model: value stream maps, capability maps and more.
how: Pick a view; it is drawn from the model each time.
tab:Business views.example: The value stream map of Handle a claim.

tab:By entity type.what: The same results grouped by entity type.
how: Open a type to see its entities.

tab:By person.what: The same list grouped by person.
how: Open a person to see their items.
Open a skill to see who has it.

tab:Calendar.what: The project's calendar: meetings, reviews, gates and deadlines.
how: ＋ Event to add one; subscribe to see it in your own calendar.

tab:Change documents.what: Documents that record changes to this model: asked, decided and done.
how: Open one to read, comment or approve.

tab:Changes.what: Uncommitted changes in this model: yours and others', waiting to be committed.
how: Commit your own; committers commit or send back others'. History shows the commits made.
tab:Changes.example: Commit your three new applications with a message.

tab:Charter.what: The project charter: purpose, scope, goals and outcomes, sponsor and stakeholders.
how: Edit the parts, then Approve the charter (the sponsor) to start the work.

tab:Close names.what: Entities whose names are close enough to be the same thing.
how: Confirm or reject each pair; confirmed ones are matched.
Add concerns in their words; link them to the views that answer them.

tab:Connect.what: How to connect an AI app to EA Explorer: the MCP address and the sign-in.
how: Copy the address into your AI app's connector settings; sign in when the browser asks.

tab:Containers.what: The Docker containers that make up EA Explorer, with state, health and resources.
how: Restart a container, read its logs or open a terminal (IT Admins).

tab:Content framework.what: The project's deliverables and artifacts by TOGAF content framework area.
how: Open an area to see what the project delivers there and its status.

tab:Custom views.what: Views made by people: drawn views and saved generated views.
how: + New drawn view; open one in its own tab; copy any view. Kind shows Drawn or Generated.

tab:Data entry.what: Add and change entities one at a time in a form.
how: Choose a type, then + New or open an entity; Save keeps it as your uncommitted change.
tab:Data entry.example: New Application Component 'Quote Engine', owner Claims IT.

tab:Deliverables and artifacts.what: The documents and artifacts the project produces.
how: Open one to see it, its versions and its sign-off.
Edit to change them; links in Link attributes open when clicked.
+ Note a discussion: when, who and what was agreed.

tab:Documents.what: Documents of the project or model.
how: Open, download or add documents.

tab:ER diagram.what: The metamodel as an entity-relationship diagram: types and the relationships allowed between them.
how: Zoom and drag; click a type to see its attributes.

tab:Elements.what: The elements found, in a list.
how: Filter by type or name; open one to see it.

tab:Engagement.what: How the project engages a stakeholder: how often, how and who keeps in touch.
how: Set the channel and frequency; note the next contact.

tab:Enterprise Repository (Project Scope.what: The part of the enterprise repository this project uses and produces.
how: Open an area to see the documents filed there.

tab:Entity types.what: The model's entity types with how many entities each has.
how: Open a type to see its entities and attributes.

tab:Every survey.what: Every survey in the installation (Super Admins).
how: Open any survey to see its state and results.
Search, then change a person's roles.

tab:Failing checks.what: Entities that fail the model's checks: required values missing, wrong values, broken rules.
how: Open an entity to fix it; Recalculate after fixing.

tab:Family.what: The model's family: its parent, children and copies.
how: Open any of them; reparent or detach from Wizards.

tab:Find in the model.what: Search the model from the drawing and drop what you find onto the canvas.
how: Type a name (near spellings work); drag a result onto the drawing.
tab:Find in the model.example: Type 'claims platfrom' to find Claims Platform.

tab:Gaps and comparison.what: Gap analyses and comparisons of the project's models.
how: + New gap analysis: baseline against target; each gap can become a work package.

tab:Governance log.what: The project's governance decisions, dispensations and compliance reviews.
how: ＋ Log a decision; send it for approval; evidence is kept with it.

tab:Graph.what: The model drawn as a graph of entities and relationships.
how: Start from an entity, choose how far to follow, zoom and drag.

tab:Grid.what: Entities of a type in a spreadsheet-like table.
how: Click a cell to edit; Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V; filter columns; changes are your uncommitted changes.
tab:Grid.example: Fill the Owner column for every application.

how: Recalculate to check again; open a red one to see why.
Open and close branches; drag to move under another parent (if you may change the model).
Pick an entry to see before and after.

tab:Home.what: The project at a glance: phase, progress, what needs you and recent activity.
how: Follow the links to the work waiting.
＋ New survey; open one to design, send, remind, close or see results.

tab:Import and export.what: Loading and downloading content: Excel and CSV sheets, deliveries from other systems, and empty templates.
how: Download a sheet, fill it, upload it: a preview shows new, changed and problem rows before it loads. Deliveries lists files sent by other systems for review.
tab:Import and export.example: Load 30 applications from an Excel sheet.

tab:KPIs.what: The model's key figures month by month and at every tag, as trends.
how: Click a KPI for its breakdown; Model Admins add their own KPIs.

tab:Key questions.what: The questions the project must answer, who asks them and the views that answer them.
how: + Add a key question; link views; mark the answer when decided.

tab:Keycloak role mapping.what: How Keycloak roles and directory groups become EA Explorer roles.
how: Map a role or group to a global role; Save.

tab:Library.what: The project's library: project pages, reference material and the enterprise reference library.
how: Pick a sub-tab; link items into the project.

tab:Licences.what: The open-source products EA Explorer runs and their licences.
how: Read only.
Pick a service; filter by words; download.

tab:Machine access.what: Tokens, API keys, client certificates and service accounts other systems use to call EA Explorer.
how: New token: pick areas (read or read-write) and an expiry; the secret is shown once. Revoke any time.
tab:Machine access.example: A read-only token for Power BI.

how: Choose the source and target; review each change before it goes in.

tab:Merge requests.what: Children sent for merge into this model, and this model's own requests.
how: Open a request to review and merge it.

tab:Metamodel.what: The model's metamodel: entity types, attributes and allowed relationships.
how: Model Admins change it through a draft: changes are reviewed before they apply.
tab:Metamodel.example: Add the attribute 'Hosting' to Application Component.

tab:Metamodel drafts.what: Proposed metamodel changes waiting for review.
how: Open a draft to comment, approve or reject.
Open a report; filter by model.

tab:Models.what: Models used by the project and the role each plays (baseline, target, scenario...).
how: Add or select models; open one to work in it.
Add a note; newest first.
Open one to act on it.
Finished items can be cleared.

tab:On the projects' Organisation tabs.what: Organisation units and people as recorded on each project's Organisation tab.
how: Open a project to change its organisation.

tab:Operations.what: Usage, housekeeping and database health (IT and Super Admins).
how: Usage: who uses what. Housekeeping: retention rules with a dry run to confirm. Database health: largest tables, slowest queries.

tab:Organisation.what: The organisation units and people relevant to the project.
how: Add units and people; link them to stakeholders.

tab:Other views and documents.what: Sample document templates to download, and files the project team uploads.
how: ⬆ Upload files; replace keeps the earlier version; download any file or template.

tab:People.what: Who has which role on this model or project.
how: Give a person access with a role; take it away when no longer needed.

tab:Phases.what: The ADM phases of the project and their steps.
how: Open a phase; tick steps done; add your own steps.

tab:Position.what: Where a stakeholder stands: power, interest and attitude.
how: Set power and interest; the stakeholder map places them.
＋ Add a principle (from the library or your own); open one for its rationale and implications.
Open a page; add pages if you may.

tab:Project report.what: A report of the project: status, phases, deliverables, decisions.
how: Download as Word or PDF.
Open one.

tab:Properties.what: All attributes and relationships of the shape selected on the drawing.
how: Edit opens the form (committers); placeholders get a type and a bind choice.

tab:Push down.what: Pushing metamodel or content changes from this model to its children.
how: Choose what to push and to which children; each child gets the change to accept.

tab:Quality.what: Data quality: score, completeness, rules passed, freshness, orphans and duplicates, drilling down to entities.
how: Open any tile to see the entities behind it; Duplicates finds and merges likely duplicates.
tab:Quality.example: Completeness 82%: open it to see what is missing.

tab:Reference.what: Reference material linked to the project.
how: Open or link reference items.
Add a relationship; open the related entity.

tab:Relationship types.what: The kinds of relationships in the model and how many of each.
how: Open a type to see where it is used.

tab:Relationships.what: The selected entity's relationships in the model, grouped by type and direction; those already on the drawing are marked.
how: Click one to put the related entity on the drawing with its line.

tab:Reports.what: Reports and dashboards on the model, the report designer, the OData feed and KPIs.
how: Open a report; the report designer builds your own; copy the OData address for Excel or Power BI.
Open one to see its answer or withdraw it.
Open one to answer it.

tab:Restores.what: Every restore and its status and log.
how: Open one to read its log.
Download them to Excel for analysis.

tab:Run a command.what: Run an eax command from the web (IT Admins).
how: Pick or type the command; its output shows below.

tab:SQL.what: Read-only SQL on the reporting views.
how: Write a SELECT and run it.

tab:Scenarios.what: Scenario models of the project compared with the baseline, and recorded assessments.
how: Open a scenario to see what it adds, changes and retires; assessments are kept as SCN-nnn with a Word document.

tab:Sheets.what: The project's tracking sheets: tables edited in place.
how: ＋ New sheet or load one from Excel or CSV; filter and download.

tab:Sign-off.what: Deliverables waiting for sign-off and decisions made.
how: Approve, reject or record a decision with evidence.

tab:Stakeholders.what: The project's stakeholders: who, position, concerns and engagement.
how: + Add a stakeholder; open one to fill in the details.

tab:Standard views.what: Views generated from the model: the same picture each time, always up to date.
how: Open one; Save as a drawn view to change it by hand.

tab:Standards.what: Standards that apply to the project.
how: ＋ Add a standard; open one for its details.
Tick steps as they are done; add your own.

tab:System settings.what: Installation settings for IT and Super Admins: services, servers, mail-free notifications, security.
how: Change and Save; switching a service on or off starts or stops it.

tab:Tags.what: Tags: named moments of the model you can go back to, compare and restore.
how: 🏷 Tag the model now; compare or download as at a tag.

tab:Tasks.what: The project's tasks with owners, status and dates.
how: ＋ New task; change status by dragging or from the task.
Open a template; use it for a new item.

tab:Templates/documents not in use.what: Templates and documents switched off for this project.
how: Mark one needed again to bring it back.

tab:Terminal.what: A terminal inside a container (IT Admins).
how: Type commands; End session when done.
Open one and answer; Save keeps a draft; Send my answers finishes it.

tab:Tools.what: What the AI assistant can do through MCP.
how: Read the list; changing tools always preview first and need a confirmation.
Open and close branches.

tab:Uncommitted changes.what: Your changes made on the drawing that are not committed yet.
how: Commit them, or open one to see it.
Search a person; change their roles.

tab:Views.what: Views: drawn views made by people and standard views generated from the model.
how: Custom views lists drawn and saved views; Standard views the generated ones; open a drawn view in its own tab.

tab:Who.what: Who the stakeholder is: name, role, organisation and contact.
how: Fill in the details.

tab:Wizards.what: Guided jobs: each explains what it does and asks before changing anything.
how: Pick a wizard card; follow its steps.

tab:▦ Map.what: The items drawn as a map.
how: Zoom and click an item to open it.

tab:✉ New request.what: Send a request to someone: what you ask for, by when.
how: Fill in the ask and Send.
Pick a tag or make a new one.

tab:Duplicates.what: Likely duplicates in the model: entities of one type with the same or close names, or the same values in attributes you choose.
how: Choose an entity type (type a few letters to find it) and how close the names must be.
Tick attributes to match on as well, for example Vendor and Version.
Press Find duplicates. Nothing found says so, with what was searched.
Download the result with Excel, or open a group with Compare and merge.
tab:Duplicates.example: Every entity type, close names: "Claims Platform" and "Claims Platfrom" come up as one group, 93% alike.

tab:OData.what: The model's OData feed address, for Power BI and Excel.
how: Copy the address; in Excel: Data › Get Data › OData feed; sign in with your user name and password, or a token as the password.

tab:Report designer.what: Build your own report: a type, its columns, related types and filters, then make the chart in the reporting tool.
how: Pick the type and columns; add related types and filters; preview; Save and open.
tab:Report designer.example: Applications with their capabilities and annual cost.

tab:Send for merge.what: Send this child model's changes to its parent for review and merge.
how: See what changed since its starting point; add a note; Send. The parent's people review each change.

tab:Updates.what: Moving EA Explorer to a newer release: the installed version, channels (Prod, RC, Latest), versions with their notes, and the history of updates and rollbacks.
how: Pick a channel and a version above the one installed; Update now or at a time. Everything is backed up first; a failed step stops and asks Retry or Roll back.

tab:Scaling.what: How many API and job servers run: a fixed number, or rules by people active and CPU.
how: Choose fixed or by rules; set the fewest and most servers, people per server, CPU limits and the cool-down; Save. The operations helper applies them every minute and lists each change.
tab:Scaling.example: 2 to 6 servers, one per 40 people active.

popup:* backup schedule.what: When backups of this kind are taken and how long they are kept.
how: Set the time and how many to keep; Save. Pinned backups are never removed.

popup:* change* clash with content commi.what: Your changes touch things someone else committed after you started.
how: For each clash choose yours or theirs (or All mine / All theirs), then Commit with these choices.

popup:* made.what: The new credential's secret. It is shown only once.
how: Copy it now and keep it safe (a password manager); then I have kept it. If lost, make a new one.

popup:* of *.what: The details of one housekeeping run (or dry run): what each rule found or did.
how: Read the counts per rule; a dry run changes nothing.

popup:*: no longer a library project.what: Stop this project being a library project, so new projects can no longer copy from it.
how: Give a reason and confirm; projects already made from it keep what they copied.

popup:A migration plan in *.what: A migration plan deliverable: work packages and transition steps from the baseline to the target.
how: Pick the gap analysis it builds on; add work packages; Save.

popup:A model from a metamodel workbook.what: Make a new model from a metamodel workbook (entity types, attributes, allowed relationships).
how: Download the empty template or a model's metamodel; fill it in Excel; upload it.
Choose blank or added to an existing model (it only adds, never takes away); check the preview; Make the model.

popup:A new event.what: Add an event to the project calendar.
how: Topic, start and end, who, where; Save. People can subscribe to the calendar.

popup:A new folder.what: Add a folder to organise documents.
how: Give it a name and where it sits; Save.

tab:Self-test.title: Self-test
tab:Self-test.what: Tests this installation: the Smoke test or the Full test, with their history and reports, and the test data they made. Super Admins and IT Admins.
how: Run: two choices. Smoke test: every role signs in, every main area answers, every page opens and the key journeys work once. Full test: every API endpoint as every role, the database, security, then every page and journey in a browser.

Each run removes the test data earlier runs left, starts a test container of its own, makes the data it needs (self_test_<id>_<n>), tests, writes the report and removes the container. Nothing else changes.
Follow it live: its step and counts; Stop ends it at its next step.
History: open a run's results; each failure says why, with what was asked and what came back, or a screenshot or video; download its report as HTML or Excel.
Test data: delete what runs made, for good, one item, one run or all of it; the reports stay.
From the command line: eax test (smoke), eax test full, eax test clean. The runs show here too.
tab:Self-test.example: A smoke test before and after an update; detailed API tests as architect after changing roles.

tab:Run.title: Run a self-test
tab:Run.what: Choose what to test and start it now (runs are never scheduled). The same runs start with eax test.
how: Smoke test: a few minutes: every role signs in, every main area answers, the key journeys work once.
Detailed tests: tick the suites (or All); Role and Area narrow them.
Watch it in this browser: the browser journeys run in this page, in this browser, while you watch (keep the page open).
Start: it shows how long it takes and asks to confirm.
tab:Run.example: Detailed, API only, role architect, area models.

popup:Start the self-test now?.what: Confirms the self-test you chose and says roughly how long it takes.
how: Start now runs it at once in its own fixtures; nothing else changes.
Cancel goes back to the choices.

how: Show and Suite filter the results.
Open What was asked and what came back under a failed API check; Screenshot and Video for a failed journey.
Download report (HTML) or Excel for the whole run.

popup:Stop self-test *?.what: Stops the running self-test at its next step.
how: It keeps what it has found so far and revokes its test accounts' tokens; its fixtures stay until you purge them.

popup:Delete * self-test fixture(s) for.what: Purges the chosen self-test fixtures: a hard delete that cannot be undone.
how: Type DELETE, then Delete for good.
Models go with everything in them (history included), projects with their documents, and the test accounts with their credentials; only what the self-test recorded is touched.
It runs as a background task; its progress shows on the page and in the task drawer.

button:Stop it: Stop the self-test at its next step; what it found so far is kept.

tab:Deploy.what: Deploying EA Explorer from this installation to another place: a server reached over SSH (Docker installed if missing), or a machine in AWS, Azure or DigitalOcean, created from your credentials or one you have. This installation is not changed.
how: Answer where and how (the same questions as eax deploy), paste or choose the SSH private key, and give the cloud credentials when a machine is to be created.
Show the plan first: it lists every step and command and runs nothing. Then Deploy.
Follow the steps and the log; a step that fails asks Retry, Back to the answers, or Quit. The run goes on if you leave the page.
Targets lists every place deployed to; Every deployment lists plans and deployments. Managing many installations together comes in release 2.
tab:Deploy.example: Deploy v0.19.0 to a new DigitalOcean Droplet for ea.fynbos-mutual.example, after checking the plan.

field:SSH private key: The OpenSSH private key (no passphrase) the target is reached with. Used for this deployment only unless you tick Keep; never shown again.
field:-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----: Paste the whole SSH private key here, from -----BEGIN to -----END.
field:Or choose the key file: Choose the SSH private key file instead of pasting it (e.g. id_ed25519). It is read in the browser and sent for this deployment only.
field:Use credentials kept for a target: Use the SSH key and cloud credentials kept from an earlier deployment to that target, instead of giving them again.
button:Show the plan (runs nothing): List every step and every command the deployment would run, without running anything.
button:Deploy: Start the deployment as the answers say (asks to confirm). It runs in the operations helper; you can leave the page.
button:Retry this step: Run the failed step again (after fixing what it said, e.g. the DNS name or the firewall).
button:Back to the answers: Back to the questions, with your answers kept, to change them and plan or deploy again.
button:Quit: Stop the deployment here. What was made so far stays; the log says how far it got.

how: Write the message, choose the level (information, notice or urgent) and, if you like, a link and the times it shows.

how: New schedule: choose the command and its options, then when it runs (every night, every week, every hour, once, or a cron expression).
A command that deletes everything needs a Super Admin and the installation's name typed once, when the schedule is made.
Turn a schedule off and on, run it now, or remove it; every run is in the History.
